facts.fact: AdWave states that paid boosts for a food truck's social posts can start at a few dollars a day, and that $5 to $10 a day targeted to a metro can meaningfully grow a local following.
facts.quote: even $5 to $10 a day targeted to your metro can meaningfully grow your local following.

facts.fact: AdWave states that a food truck's Google Ads budget of even $10 to $15 a day can capture meaningful local search traffic.
facts.quote: even $10 to $15 a day can capture meaningful local search traffic.

facts.fact: AdWave states that organic posting on Instagram and TikTok is free.
AdWave states that a Google Business Profile is free to set up and maintain.
facts.quote: Free to set up and maintain.

facts.fact: AdWave describes connected TV advertising as letting a food truck run a real 30-second video ad on premium streaming channels.
facts.quote: lets you run a real 30-second video ad on premium streaming channels

facts.fact: AdWave's article is titled as a 2026 guide and carries a published time of July 4, 2026.
Adwave's pricing page says customers can get started from $30 a day.
facts.quote: check [pricing](https://adwave.com/pricing) to get started from $30 a day.

facts.fact: Adwave states it can generate a 30-second ad from a customer's photos and website.
facts.quote: generate a mouth-watering 30-second ad from your photos and website

facts.fact: The page states that Instagram and TikTok boosted posts start at about $5 per day, with organic posting free.
The page states that Google Ads starts at about $10 to $15 per day for food truck advertising.
The page's common approach suggests food trucks add $5 to $15 a day on paid social boosts or Google Ads, after free organic Instagram and Google Business Profile use.
facts.quote: add $5 to $15 a day on paid social boosts or Google Ads

facts.fact: The page lists Google Business Profile as having no starting cost for food trucks.
facts.quote: Google Business Profile | Being found in "near me" searches | Good | Free

facts.fact: The page lists local events and partnerships as free to the vendor apart from vendor fees.
